chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, who said: Abu Khalid al-Ka'bi narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Any woman who moves something in the house of her husband from one place to another, wanting to improve it, Allah looks upon her - and whoever Allah looks upon, He does not punish. So Umm Salama said: Men have taken all the good, so what is there for poor women? He said: Rather, when a woman becomes pregnant, she has the status of one who fasts, prays, and strives. When she gives birth, she receives an incomprehensible reward. When she breastfeeds, each suckle equals freeing a descendant of Isma'il. When she finishes, an angel strikes her side: Continue working, Allah has forgiven you.

key_terms.استأنفي العمل: Continue working - the angel's command after breastfeeding ends, signaling a clean slate
key_terms.بمنزلة الصائم القائم المجاهد: Of the status of fasting, praying, and striving - the triple reward of pregnancy
key_terms.كعدل عتق محرر: Like freeing a freed slave - the reward for each breastfeeding session

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the reward of motherhood?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (S) elevates the status of women by honoring domestic care, then responds to Umm Salama's concern about women's share of good by describing the immense spiritual rewards of motherhood: pregnancy equals fasting, prayer, and jihad; childbirth brings incomprehensible reward; breastfeeding earns reward equivalent to freeing a noble slave with each suckle; and upon weaning, an angel announces complete forgiveness.
